brief_summary: This study is a prospective randomized study to examine the effects of exposure to dulaglutide on the prevention of stress-hyperglycemia and the metabolic inflammatory response in the perioperative period.
brief_title: Metabolic Phenotyping During Stress Hyperglycemia in Cardiac Surgery Patients
collaborators: National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS)

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Males or females between the ages of 40 and 80 years
* Body mass index (BMI) ≥25
* Undergoing elective CABG surgery
* No previous history of diabetes or hyperglycemia

Exclusion Criteria:

* Hyperglycemia (BG\>125 mg/dl or HbA1c \> 6.5%) or previous treatment with antidiabetic agents
* Impaired renal function (GFR \< 30 ml/min) or clinically significant hepatic failure
* Gastrointestinal obstruction expected to require gastrointestinal suction
* Patients with clinically relevant pancreatic or gallbladder disease
* Treatment with oral or injectable corticosteroid
* Mental condition rendering the subject unable to understand the possible consequences of the study
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding at time of enrollment

official_title: Metabolic Phenotyping During Stress Hyperglycemia in Cardiac Surgery Patients

primary_outcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Blood Glucose Levels (BG) > 140 mg/dl During Post Operative Period
primary_outcomes.time_frame: During the hospital stay (up to 12 days postoperatively)

why_stopped: The study was terminated following the Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) review due to concerns with perioperative use of the study drug.
